title: Subarrays & Substrings
overview:
What is a Subarray?
A subarray is a continuous part of an array.

For example:

Array:       [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

Subarrays:       [2] [3] [4]
             [3] [4]
                 [3] [4] [5]

The elements in a subarray must be next to each other in the original array.

For an array:

[1, 2, 3]

[1, 2] is a subarray, but [1, 3] is not a subarray because 2 is skipped.

What is a Substring?
A substring is a continuous part of a string.

For example:

String:       "ABCDE"

Substring:     "BCD"

"BCD" is a substring because its characters appear continuously in the original string.

But "BDE" is not a substring because the characters are not continuous.

Subarray vs Substring
The main difference is the type of data they come from:

Array  → Subarray
String → Substring

Both must contain continuous elements/characters.

importantConcepts.title: Continuous Elements
importantConcepts.description:
The most important property is continuity.

[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

[2, 3, 4]  → Subarray ✅
[2, 4]      → Not a subarray ❌

importantConcepts.title: Subarray / Substring vs Subsequence
importantConcepts.description:
These concepts are often confused.

A subarray or substring must be continuous.
A subsequence does not need to be continuous, but the original order must be maintained.

Array:       [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Subarray:    [2, 3, 4]  → continuous
Subsequence: [2, 4, 5]  → not continuous

For strings:

String:      "ABCDE"

Substring:   "BCD"  → continuous
Subsequence: "ACE"  → not continuous

importantConcepts.title: Number of Possible Subarrays / Substrings
importantConcepts.description:
For an array or string containing n elements/characters, the total number of non-empty subarrays or substrings is:

n × (n + 1) / 2

For example, an array of 4 elements has:

4 × 5 / 2 = 10

non-empty subarrays.

This becomes useful when solving problems involving all possible subarrays or substrings.

howItWorks: A subarray or substring can be identified using its starting and ending positions.

For an array:

Array: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
        0   1   2   3   4

The subarray from index 1 to 3 is:

[20, 30, 40]

Similarly, for a string:

String: "HELLO"
Index:   0 1 2 3 4

The substring from index 1 to 3 is:

"ELL"
So, we can think of a subarray or substring as a continuous range between two positions.

complexity.time: Generating or checking all possible subarrays/substrings can involve O(n²) possibilities. If we actually process the elements of every subarray/substring, the total work can become O(n³) with a straightforward approach.
complexity.space: Storing a particular subarray or substring requires space proportional to its length, up to O(n).
notes: There isn't one fixed complexity for every subarray/substring problem. It depends on what we are doing with them.

keyTakeaways: A subarray is a continuous part of an array.
A substring is a continuous part of a string.
Both are defined by a continuous range of positions.
A subsequence does not need to be continuous, unlike a subarray or substring.
An array or string of n elements has n(n+1)/2 non-empty subarrays or substrings.
Subarray and substring concepts are important foundations for techniques like prefix sum, sliding window, and two pointers.
